runs.note: Serialized and uncontended. 75 -> 9 failures. The 9 are exactly the RC-C residual already classified: control_registry 5, mutator_registry 1, and one each in exp3_harness / exp0004_harness / exp0004_blinding.

triage.note: 75 failures, 2 dominant root causes, both attributable to commit 1c1f68d (#48, selector made load-bearing in the live gate). Neither was visible while the 280s ceiling truncated the run.

root_causes.cause: build-os/runtime/MANIFEST.json pins sha256 0b83040575 for .claude/hooks/routing-gate.sh; the file is now f2364d3f50. The manifest was last re-cut at 04e602a, BEFORE 1c1f68d edited the gate. The first assertion fails and every install/verify assertion cascades from it.
root_causes.resolution: OPERATOR DECISION. `regen-manifest` requires --version <v>: by the runtime tool's own design, re-cutting the manifest IS cutting a release. A worker must not pick a version number unilaterally.
root_causes.verified: 7 of 8 manifest entries match; exactly 1 drifted.

root_causes.cause: 1c1f68d made the gate GENERATE its refusal from the authority selector. Under the default host profile unknown_conservative, Bash is approval_required, so the selector correctly advertises the Write-class routing-request channel and states the shell path is NOT AVAILABLE. Three suites extract a `route-task.sh ... --descriptor` command from the refusal text; the extraction now returns empty, so `eval "$RCMD --out ..."` runs `--out` as a command.
root_causes.the_real_defect: The tests and the demo encode a HOST PROFILE they never declare: they assume a host where Bash is usable. That is the same class as authority_bootstrap_permission_class_mismatch from EXP-0005 -- a permission-lattice assumption baked in implicitly rather than stated. The gate's new behaviour is arguably CORRECT: advertising a path the host will refuse is what the selector exists to prevent, and capability-discoverable-at-failure requires advertising VIABLE paths, not all paths.
root_causes.resolution: OPERATOR DECISION, because the two readings lead to different fixes. (a) The refusal should still carry a shell recovery command -- then the selector's host-conditional advertising is the regression. (b) The tests and demo should declare a host profile in which Bash is viable, and assert against the refusal the selector generates for THAT profile -- then the product is right and three suites encode a superseded contract.

root_causes.cause: TRIAGED INDIVIDUALLY. Four distinct causes, not one.
root_causes.resolution: 2 fixed, 3 blocked by a standing constraint, 5 pre-existing debt (2 of which were mine and are fixed).

classified.evidence: Same undeclared-host-profile assumption as RC-B: the suite left GRAVITO_HOST_PROFILE unset (meaning unknown_conservative, Bash approval-gated, no approver) and then asserted the refusal carries a route-task.sh shell command. Declaring claude_code_interactive for the block that measures shell recovery: 122/2 -> 124/0.

All three assert 'no executable files under build-os/experiments/'. The sole offender is build-os/experiments/EXP-0005-system-efficiency/harness/restore-seed.sh, tracked at mode 100755. It is a FROZEN EXP-0005 artifact, and the standing instruction forbids altering, rewriting, deleting, regenerating or rerunning any frozen EXP-0005 artifact. chmod would modify it.
classified.note: NOT a defect this worker may clear. Resolving it requires either an operator act unfreezing that one file's mode, or an explicit allow-list entry in the three suites. Both are operator decisions; neither is taken here.

triage.coverage_caveat: This triage is from ONE completed run. It establishes that the suite CAN finish and that it is red; it does not establish which failures are deterministic. A second run is needed before any failure is called stable or flaky.

determinism_note: Two completed runs now exist, 536s and 533s, so the DURATION is repeatable. They are NOT a repeat measurement of the same tree -- the second ran against 65 fixed failures -- so no failure has yet been shown deterministic. That still needs two runs at one HEAD.
